newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - March 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - March 4.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on March 4. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
President Suharto has asked that better and more certain services be given to the 200,000 Indonesians who will undertake the Islamic haj pilgrimage to the holy lands in Saudi Arabia this year.

The weak capitalisation of Indonesia's banks and insurance companies will inhibit them from competing in other countries in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) when the financial services within the group are liberalised, bank executives said.

Legislators in the national parliament have asked that three telecommunications consortiums, each containing a foreign partner, which have not reached their targets for the connection of new telephone lines be punished with sanctions.
Indonesia posted a trade surplus of $961.1 million in December 1996, down from $1.020 billion in December 1995, a Department of Industry and Trade document said.

Prosecutors in the central Java city of Yogyakarta have for the fourth time returned a police dossier on a suspect alleged to have committed the high profile murder of a local journalist as the dossier is said to be deficient.
Armed forces chief General Fiesal Tanjung said the military will "clobber" any group or person who wants to destabilise the national leadership.

Police have said it is still possible that ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri could be called as a suspect in an investigation into an alleged illegal meeting held at her house in January. Thousands demonstrated outside South Jakarta police headquarters during her second round of questioning on Monday.
